title: Veterinary and Pet Care Business
desc: Start and run a small pet care business, from grooming, boarding and walking to records, hygiene and when to refer to a vet.
outcomes: Explain animal welfare needs and the limits of a non-vet service.
Run safe handling, hygiene and booking steps.
Judge risks, bites, disease and legal duties.
task: Plan and pilot a small pet care service with welfare rules, hygiene plan, booking and price sheet, owner forms and emergency steps.
condition: Practice animals from willing owners or a shelter partner, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor veterinarian. Medical treatments are for qualified vets only.
standard: Every pet has an owner form and vaccine record; welfare needs are met; injuries and bites have a response plan; costs and price are shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Pet lovers, vet clinic assistants, groomers, walkers and boarders.
evidence: service menu, owner form, hygiene plan, price sheet, pilot log
modules: Five needs: food and water, shelter, health, behaviour and company.
Know species needs and daily routines.
Signs of stress: panting, hiding, aggression.
Never leave animals in hot vehicles.
A dog left in shade with fresh water stays calm; one in a parked car does not.
Write a welfare card for two species.
Know the pet before you take it.
Name, age, vaccines, medicines, allergies, vet contact, emergency contact.
Written consent for care and emergency treatment.
A boarding form shows an unvaccinated pup, so it is declined.
Use correct leads and carriers; keep species apart.
First-aid for bites and scratches; report them.
A walker uses a double lead near traffic.
Clean and disinfect kennels, tools and bowls between animals.
A cough in one dog leads to isolation and a vet call.
When to refer to a vet
Poisoning, injury, breathing trouble, long vomiting, seizures need a vet at once.
Do not give medicines unless a vet or owner instructs in writing.
A boarder calls the vet within 10 minutes for a dog that ate chocolate.
Includes numbers, steps and owner contacts.
Grooming, walking, boarding, day care; time per pet.
Costs: staff, supplies, transport, insurance, space.
Price to cover costs and margin.
A 60-minute groom has 90 minutes of table time.
Business licence, animal-welfare rules and insurance.
No cruelty or neglect; report abuse.
A provider obtains public-liability insurance before taking clients.
Run 30 days with a few clients.
Plan owner education and community tie-ups.
Rebookings reach 55% after report cards with photos.
